::: {.why}
Everything you learned in week 8 applies to a grid search, and the standard workflow of picking the best cross-validated configuration is exactly the procedure your noise floor was built to correct.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Say what selecting the best of N hyperparameter configurations does to the cross-validated estimate, and quantify it for your own search.
- Implement nested validation so the selection and the evaluation use different data.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Measure the selection bias: run your grid on pure-noise labels and report the best cross-validated R-squared it finds. That number is the bias in your reported figure for a grid of that size, and it is subtracted rather than argued about.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Implement nested validation in qlib/ml/: an inner purged split for hyperparameter selection and an outer walk-forward split for evaluation, so the number you report was never used for selection. Rerun both models and report the difference against the non-nested figures.
:::
:::
